title: Local connectivity balance shapes population dynamics in random recurrent networks
authors: Shotaro Takasu, Richard Gast, Ann Kennedy
abstract: Disordered dynamical systems comprising many interacting units, from ecological communities to neural circuits, are ubiquitous, and understanding how connectivity shapes their collective behavior is a central theoretical challenge. One long-recognized feature of neural circuits is local connectivity balance, in which the excitatory and inhibitory weights converging onto each unit approximately cancel. Although local connectivity balance has been proposed to serve functions such as gating incoming signals, its effect on collective network dynamics remains unclear. Here we analytically study randomly connected recurrent networks with varying degrees of local connectivity balance. We show that this balance leaves the connectivity spectrum unchanged yet drastically reshapes the dynamics in a manner that depends critically on the single-unit nonlinearity. Local balance suppresses unbounded growth of the network state and stabilizes network dynamics when the activation function scales linearly or faster, whereas it drives the network into chaos when the activation function is sub-linear or saturating. Importantly, these effects vanish for odd activation functions, which are commonly assumed in previous work. We further find that, for saturating nonlinearities, the effective dimension of the dynamics varies nonmonotonically with the degree of balance. We show that all these phenomena arise from a unifying mechanism: the suppression of a self-generated feedback input by local connectivity balance. Our results identify local connectivity balance as a previously overlooked control parameter for collective dynamics in realistic disordered networks.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes how local connectivity balance ($\mu$) controls the collective dynamics of random recurrent neural networks. It shows that $\mu$ acts as a switch: stabilizing dynamics for certain nonlinearities while inducing chaos for others. The work establishes $\mu$ as a crucial, previously overlooked control parameter for understanding complex disordered systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how the statistical structure of connectivity, specifically 'local connectivity balance,' shapes the collective dynamics of disordered recurrent networks.
main_result: Local connectivity balance acts as a critical control parameter: it stabilizes dynamics for linear/supra-linear nonlinearities but drives the network into chaos for sub-linear/saturating ones.
method: The analysis employs analytical techniques, including the path-integral formalism, saddle-point approximation, and dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) in the limit N -> infinity.
model_or_system: The model is a randomly connected recurrent network governed by a differential equation involving a unit nonlinearity $\phi(x)$. The key structural element is the local connectivity balance parameter $\mu$.
key_observables: Network state divergence, stability (fixed point vs. chaos), Maximum Lyapunov Exponent (MLE), and the effective dimension (Participation Ratio).
important_parameters: Local connectivity balance parameter ($\mu$), the single-unit nonlinearity ($\phi(x)$), and the coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the saddle-point approximation in the limit N -> infinity, and previous work often incorrectly assumed the activation function must be odd.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the effect of $\mu$ on stability (e.g., ReLU vs. Sigmoid), show MLE changes, and map out phase diagrams showing critical coupling strengths ($g_c$) dependent on $\mu$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the system and the role of $\mu$, deriving the generating functional via path integrals, applying the saddle-point approximation to find order parameters, and finally analyzing the resulting mean-field equations to determine stability regimes based on the nonlinearity type.
why_interesting: The findings establish a deep connection between structural constraints (local balance) and dynamical stability, providing a general framework applicable to complex, non-equilibrium dynamics found in many-body physics.
